The planet humans live on is Earth.

To help comprehend Heisenberg's Uncertainty Principle, consider the analogy provided: trying to walk through a crowded room with your eyes closed. In this scenario, your focus on avoiding physical contact (determining position) inherently limits your awareness of the speed and direction of the people around you (momentum). Just as you cannot simultaneously know exactly where everyone is and how fast they are moving in that chaotic environment, in quantum mechanics, you cannot precisely measure both the position and momentum of a particle at the same time. The more precisely you determine one, the less precisely you can know the other.
